name: Pilha
overview: Pilha is a male figure mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as a non-Levite leader. He is named specifically in the sealed document of Nehemiah 10:1-27, highlighting his role among the signatories. Although his tribal affiliation is not specified, his leadership position is notable in the post-exilic community.
namesAndTitles: The name Pilha means 'millstone; plowman; harelip,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name with agricultural and functional connotations. This name is not indicated as being given directly by God but is recorded in Nehemiah 10:24.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Pilha as a descendant of Jacob, establishing his Israelite heritage. Beyond this, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Pilha's significance lies in his inclusion among the leaders who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah 10, demonstrating his active participation in the community's commitment to God's law after the exile. His status as a non-Levite leader underscores the involvement of various Israelite groups in the restoration efforts, emphasizing unity under divine covenant. This highlights the collaborative nature of rebuilding both the physical and spiritual life of Israel during Nehemiah's time.
